videos.script: Lesson 16 ran routing protocols inside one network. Every router there was on the same side. {{recap}} The internet is different. It is tens of thousands of networks, run by different people. They still have to tell each other what they can reach. The protocol for that is BGP. {{bgp}} The lab is a company with its own block of addresses. It has its own autonomous system number, and two providers. {{lab}} You will open a BGP session to each provider. At first the router refuses to exchange anything. It waits until you write down what may go in and what may go out. {{session}} Then you will read the AS path. That is the list of networks a route has crossed, and it decides which way the traffic goes. {{path}} You will make the path longer on purpose. One provider will change its mind about how to reach you. {{prepend}} Then you will make a mistake on purpose. You will announce routes you should not. The filter on the other side will catch it. {{leak}} Last come the defences the real internet uses. Route filters, and signed records of who holds which addresses. {{rpki}}
